l + Infinitiv can specify what milk is ready/suitable for (aṯi l taqṭoro); temperature is inferred from the following context, not an overt cooling predicate.
Season severity stays atmospheric; masculine oṯe hawa and feminine kuṯyo i hawa in the same description deserve dialect/lexical-gender comparison.
Summer heat can affect an ʕal-marked participant; kef uses an l-suffix experiencer. The kef idiom is already recorded and is not a fresh sense.

Structural components, construction fronts and stationary fences occur in descriptions of coming next or reaching an endpoint. Roof-as-subject and process-reaching-roof clauses differ syntactically and are not silently reduced to one valency pattern.

Thoughts, ruḥo, qanaʕa, ṣabr and ʕəšq extend the state-subject inventory. The human is an l-suffix experiencer, a possessed-noun experiencer, or b- affected person; default/singular agreement with feminine/plural state nouns must remain visible.

evidence.cite: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/19

summary: Institutions, gifts, fate and electricity are arriving subjects; detached body parts and needles are moving themes. These changes of participant do not independently establish senses.

Unpersönliches k-oṯe d- can introduce the feasibility of an event, including a following Detransitive (məqrəf). The modal interpretation belongs to the whole construction, not a Detransitive form of ʔṯy.
4/8 evaluates words as yaquro to an ʕal-marked person; this extends the result-predicate evidence to how words come across, and remains a single evaluative attestation.
Crop-yield, benefit and wages are accruing themes; temporal subjects include midnight, seasons, upcoming days and turns in worship. These are not independent senses based only on subject type.
Paired coming and going can describe swinging. Human goal metaphors include former life-condition; m-source metaphors can name illness beside geographical absence.

The endurance nouns ṣabr and tabata recur with possessive experiencer or l-suffix; haw in tabata haw aṯile/koṯele must be retained as negative/no-longer material. Worry has l-experiencers plus ʕal-topic, and ftakar is a thought subject with an l-experiencer.

ʕal fəkr/xabro encodes the position or agreement to which someone conforms; personal acceptability can also take qəm diḏ- or l-ḥasab. Preserve distinctions from reciprocal agreement (4), and keep the sense-9 duty/acceptance question open.
Befall clauses with a predicament, fault, decree or head-goal belong with the event constructions; arrival of Saturday remains temporal coming, not automatically a bodily-state use.
A secure tox/tux Imperativ may introduce a suggestion or direct the listener to a scene without a literal goal. This does not resolve the separate tay/taw/tə attribution problem.

The existing mind-to-head recovery idiom has həš, hawno/hawn, ḥəs/ḥəš and alternate head noun qarʕo. Preserve source spellings and the question whether the sibilant variants represent one lexical item.
81/108 has a personal gab-goal in a paternity admission. Sexual intercourse is contextually inferred; lexicalization as a sexual euphemism is not established.
88/75 and 88/246 combine personal l-goals with b-marked implements or a stratagem. Hostility/success is supplied by the event context, rather than a separate attack or outwit sense.

The inherited awareness-subject recovery idiom gains həs diḏan li dukṯo at 91/40. Contrast the human subject aṯi l həš diḏe at 88/80; the latter has its own collocation headword. L-dukṯo here is the restored place of awareness, not fulfilment of a promise.
The memory idiom uses b boli at 77/70 beside inherited l-bol-. Preserve b- as supplied; it must not be silently normalized. Experiencer is the possessor of bol-.
b qarʕe at 91/1 and b qarʕe d tə isane at 96/164 vary inherited b-rišo/l-qarʕan in the befall/experience idiom. No duplicate idiom headword is needed.

Laughter gaxko at 95/123 extends the state-onset subjects; kef at 95/262 has experiencer -li and target -lux in a counterfactual Infectum-wa. A target suffix must not be conflated with the experiencer.

94/293–306 applies the result construction to knucklebone throws, with qimo/qime, ṭawwo/pis and named faces. 94/297 and 299 contrast completed aṯi in conditions with prospective oṯe; repeated tokens are one technical passage, not independent lexical senses.

Counting-out results at 94/346, 348 and 415 use aʕ ʕəsri or a final count-word as subject, with ʕal-goal or l-recipient. This is an abstract assignment extension, distinguished from 17 by absence of a result predicate.
97/51 has the girl herself as subject coming li ḏ̣arbo d meqəm, a restored former-state goal. This differs from state nouns as subjects (15) and from 17 with a result predicate.

Batch 5 initially treated 88/75 and 88/246 as personal l-goals with b-marked implements or a stratagem. Batch 6 establishes 21 for acting on a target and reinterprets 88/75 accordingly; 88/246 remains a manner/stratagem extension of 1.

Batch 6 overturns the purely spatial extension decision for 88/75 in batch 5: target plus bath implements is now supported by repeated action-on-target patterns in 98/64, 105/20–24 and 113/152. Its earlier occurrence decision remains the history of that batch. Hostile approach without this action pattern and manner b-i=ḥila at 88/246 remain under 1.

101/9 has u šuġlo du lalyo bi ḥalo. The supplied reader cites the carpet/floor dictionary entry; the verse does not justify silently reading bi ḥalo as in its time/state. Event arrival is retained without a new idiom or an independently inferred onset sense.
103/18,33,35 repeats the outcome maxim i taliye ... aydarbo gdəṯyo. Manner aydarbo characterizes the result and files with 17; repetition is one maxim, not three independent semantic attestations.

103/30 foṯi aṯyo ġalabe d ḥəlqatli supports a face being at the stage for shaving; whether this is a metonymic facial-hair growth construction needs confirmation. No technical grow sense is published.

The Preterit Intransitive cell now includes aʕla, full ʕal i emo and eba; triggers range from invitations/requests to deaths and verbal insult. The events are evaluated as distressing or unwelcome, not always literally difficult work.

Repeated kef passages confirm l-experiencer, a doubled l-noun plus suffix (107/28;112/8), a possessor experiencer (Talay 1/247) and an additional l-stimulus (113/3). The inherited 29/195 move to 15 is already cumulative; no duplicate correction or surplus Preterit example is needed.
